target_customer: Fashion shoppers buying from independent local boutiques, and boutique owners who sell through the marketplace
problem: Independent boutiques carried unique inventory but had little or no online presence, and shoppers could not browse many of them in one place.
business_model: Marketplace with a commission on boutique sales; later a point of sale and commerce platform for boutiques (Material)

founders.name: Olga Vidisheva
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia says she is a former Goldman Sachs investment banker and Harvard Business School graduate who surveyed over 800 boutiques while writing the business plan. She stepped back from daily operations in July 2020.

founders.name: Peter Delahunty
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder and describes him as a long term hacker.

founders.name: Dan Morin
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio.

founders.name: Jeff Morin
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: A curated multi seller storefront with inventory integration for boutiques in several cities was standard ecommerce engineering. The hard part was operational, onboarding boutiques and syncing inventory.

defensibility.rationale: Supply came from vetted boutique relationships found through magazine partnerships and referrals, but another marketplace could recruit the same boutiques. About half of applicant boutiques were rejected, which gave some curation value.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it according to sources opened. In 2022 the company was stagnating on its custom platform and moved to Shopify in March 2023 per a company published case study.

market_need_then: The March 2012 TechCrunch launch piece said many local boutiques had no online presence and only about half of applicant boutiques qualified for unique inventory. Items priced 50 to 300 dollars sold from over 25 boutiques in Los Angeles, Miami, New York and Chicago at launch.

branding.domain_note: Operates at shoptiques.com. Trademark SHOPTIQUES filed 2012-03-12 by Shoptiques LLC per a Justia listing.

identity.logo: wordmark, details not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline about shopping local and shopping the world

branding.brand_signature: Shop local boutiques from anywhere positioning

rebrands.why: Business arm that sells commerce and point of sale software to independent retailers was renamed; the consumer marketplace kept the Shoptiques name (per Wikipedia)

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage on Entrepreneur, CNBC, TechCrunch and AlleyWatch. The company reached 5,000 boutiques in 2016 per FashionNetwork. No evidence of merch or fan communities.

brand_strength.rationale: A recognizable name in boutique ecommerce with steady press over a decade and a 2012 trademark, but no source shows the brand itself driving growth.

pivots.from: Consumer marketplace with a custom built platform
pivots.to: Shopify storefront plus Material point of sale and software for independent retailers
pivots.why: Company case study says the custom platform was stagnating in 2022 and the move to Shopify went live in March 2023

outcome_analysis: Shoptiques launched in spring 2012 with top tier backers and grew to thousands of boutiques, and it is still trading in 2026. Its own case study admits a stall in 2022 on a custom platform, followed by a replatform and the Material software brand. There is no exit or shutdown. The record fits a marketplace that survived but never reached the scale its early funding implied, with later rounds not publicly confirmed.
notes: The March 21, 2012 TechCrunch piece names the five investors and says the amount was undisclosed. Aggregators disagree: Seedtable lists a 2 million dollar seed in October 2012 (single aggregator, unverified), CB Insights lists 270 thousand dollars over 4 rounds including a 250 thousand dollar PPP loan in April 2020 (aggregator, unverified). No Series A found. The TechCrunch launch article names no competitors (Etsy appears only as a comparison), so the competitor list is empty; later lists such as Trouva are not as of founding. Education and employers for Vidisheva come from Wikipedia, not the YC page.
